newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - CompUSA, 3Com rise.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - CompUSA, 3Com rise.

text.p: CompUSA Inc's report of better-than-expected quarterly earning launced a rebound in the shares early Wednesday from the prior sesssion's pounding sparked by an analyst's cautious view of computer retailing.
In Wednesday pre-open trade, CompUSA gained 1-1/2 to 53, making up part of Tuesday's 5-1/2 point decline.

Yesterday's sell-off came after Salomon Bros analyst David Childe said "industry softness, promotions and CompUSA's current inventory position are some negative issues that are now surrounding the company."
CompUSA said it earned $0.31 per share in the fiscal first quarter, or $14.5 million, versus $0.15 per share, or $6.2 million, in the year-ago period.
Revenues rose to $990 million from $782 million, and the company also reported a 7.2 percent increase in same-store sales for the 13 weeks ended September 28.
The first quarter net exceeded the Zack's consensus estimate by $0.06 per share.
3Com traded up one 63-1/2 preceding the open after the company said last night it may top its 52 to 54 percent gross margin target in upcoming quaters.
Sigma-Aldrich Corp gained one to 58-5/8 as investor interest grew after Merrill Lynch named the stock its Focus One and rated its a near-term accumulate and long-term buy.
